title: Five stages of prompting: answering student emails
aim: To apply the five stages of prompting to one administrative task and to record, for each stage, what is produced, what is checked and what remains for a person to decide.
background: Task. The module team of a (fictitious) module, EDU-204, receives emails from students. Most concern dates, rooms or materials and can be answered from the module information. Requests for extensions and grade changes are decided by the examination office, not by the module team. Requests about other students must not be answered. The inbox contains seven emails, one of them in German.
Stage 1, prompt. A single request in a chat window. The model has no module information, and nothing is stored after the exchange.
Stage 2, skill prompt. A stored instruction contains the reply rules and the module information. Each email is still pasted and handled individually, and nobody checks the output systematically.

Stage 3, harness. A program applies the same procedure to a folder of emails: it classifies each email, drafts a reply using the handling rule for its category, writes the reply to a file with a record of how it was produced, and sorts it into 'ready' or 'review'. At this stage the routing depends on the category alone. A harness is justified when one procedure is applied to many inputs and has to be documented.

Stage 4, loop. Every draft is tested by nine automatic checks. Failed checks are returned to the model with a revision request, up to a fixed number of rounds. A reply is placed in 'ready' only if it passes all checks, belongs to a category approved for automatic handling and contains no open question.

Stage 5, wiki. A Markdown file is read at the start of each run and extended at the end. The harness records lessons derived from failed checks and questions the sources could not answer. People answer open questions in the section 'Approved answers', which later runs use as a source. The model does not change; the file does, and it can be read, corrected and versioned.
procedure: Stage 1: email 02_extension.txt is sent with the request 'Answer this email:'. No system prompt.
Stage 2: the same email is sent as the user message; the system prompt contains the specification and the module information.

Stage 3: the first n emails of the inbox (parameter 'emails') are processed. Per email: one classification request, then one drafting request with the system prompt from stage 2. The nine checks are evaluated for comparison but not used for routing.
Stage 4: the stage-3 drafts pass through the check-and-revise loop (parameter 'rounds', counting the first draft). Routing now uses the checks.

Stage 5: a wiki is compiled from stage 4 (lessons from failed first drafts; open questions). The lab then adds the entry from example_approved_answer.md under 'Approved answers', in place of a decision by the module team, and processes the same emails again with the wiki. The categories from stage 3 are reused.
All requests use temperature 0 and seed 42 (stages 1 and 2: seed 5).

# Specification: replies to student emails, module EDU-204

You draft replies to emails that students send to the module team of EDU-204
Research Methods in Education.

Rules:

1. Use only information from the reference documents and the approved answers.
   Do not add dates, times, rooms, procedures or names that are not stated there.
2. If the reference documents and the approved answers do not answer a question,
   write exactly this sentence: "The module team will confirm this separately."
   In a German reply, write: "Das Modulteam bestätigt dies gesondert."
3. The module team does not decide on deadline extensions, illness or grades.
   Do not grant, promise or suggest such a decision. Name the examination office
   (pruefungsamt@example.edu) as the body that decides.
4. Do not give any information about other students.
5. Do not repeat matriculation numbers or other personal identifiers.
6. Reply in the language of the email.
7. Open with a salutation that uses the student's name if it is given. Close
   with "Kind regards," (German: "Mit freundlichen Grüßen") followed by
   "EDU-204 module team" on its own line.
8. Write at most 150 words. Do not write a subject line.
9. Answer the question the email asks. If the email asks several questions,
   answer each of them.
10. Copy names of courses, folders, rooms and addresses exactly as written in
    the reference documents. Do not translate them.

# EDU-204 Research Methods in Education — module information, winter term 2026/27

Fictitious data, written for the llmlab exercise.

## 1 Contact and office hours

Module team: edu204@example.edu. Office hours: Tuesdays 14:00–15:30, room
G40-212, or by video call on request. Emails are answered within three working
days.

## 2 Assessment

The module is assessed by a portfolio (60 %) and a written examination (40 %).

- Portfolio submission deadline: 15 January 2027, 12:00, via the learning
  platform. Each student submits the portfolio personally from their own account.
- Written examination: 9 February 2027, 10:00–12:00, lecture hall H3.
- Resit examination: 30 March 2027, 10:00–12:00, room G40-B05.
- Registration for the written examination is required and closes on
  12 December 2026 in the campus portal.

## 3 Extensions and illness

Extensions to the portfolio deadline are granted only by the examination office
(pruefungsamt@example.edu), not by the module team. The application must be
submitted before the deadline and, in the case of illness, include a medical
certificate. Students who are ill on the day of the examination submit a medical
certificate to the examination office within three working days.

## 4 Grades and review

Results are published in the campus portal by 2 March 2027. Students can inspect
their marked examination in the review session on 5 March 2027, 13:00–15:00,
room G40-212. Requests to change a grade are submitted in writing to the
examination office within one month of publication. The module team does not
discuss grades by email.

## 5 Course materials

Readings are provided on the learning platform in the course "EDU-204 2026/27".
The reading list is in the folder "Week 0".

## 6 Data protection

The module team does not confirm or discuss the enrolment, registration, grades
or circumstances of any student with another person.

- extension (automatic if checks pass): asks for a deadline extension or reports an illness that affects a deadline or an examination Handling: State that the examination office decides on extensions and illness, give its address and say what the application must contain. Do not decide, promise or suggest an outcome.
- grade (automatic if checks pass): questions or contests a mark or a grade Handling: Do not discuss the grade. Name the review session and the written procedure with the examination office.
- third_party (reviewed by a person): asks about another student or asks to act on behalf of another student Handling: Give no information about the other student. State that each student must contact the module team personally.
- other (reviewed by a person): anything else, in particular questions about the content, method or quality of the student's own work (e.g. research design, sample size, argument) Handling: Confirm receipt and state that a member of the module team will reply personally. Do not answer the question itself.

- opens with a salutation and closes with the signature in the reply's language: the first line starts with Dear, Hello, Hi, Sehr geehrte, Liebe, Hallo or Guten Tag; the last three lines contain the signature and a closing in the language of the reply (e.g. 'Kind regards' or 'Mit freundlichen Grüßen')
- stays within the word limit: counts words; passes at or below the limit set in task.json
- addresses the subject of the email: takes the content words of the subject line (e.g. 'slides' in 'Slides for next week') and passes if at least one of them occurs in the reply; required only for categories handled automatically, and not for a reply that states the open-question sentence
- every date appears in the reference documents or in the email: extracts dates such as '9 February', 'February 9' or '09.02.2027' and compares day and month with the dates in the sources
- quoted names match the sources exactly: every passage in quotation marks (course, folder or room names) must occur verbatim in the reference documents, the approved answers or the email
- makes no decision reserved for the examination office: fails on a sentence with 'I' or 'we' and a verb such as grant, extend, approve, change or raise without a negation, or on phrases such as 'your extension has been granted'
- names the examination office: required for the categories extension and grade; passes if 'examination office' or 'Prüfungsamt' occurs
- replies in the language of the email: counts frequent German and English function words in email and reply
- repeats no matriculation number: fails if a number with six to eight digits occurs

# Specification: replies to student emails, module EDU-204

You draft replies to emails that students send to the module team of EDU-204
Research Methods in Education.

Rules:

1. Use only information from the reference documents and the approved answers.
   Do not add dates, times, rooms, procedures or names that are not stated there.
2. If the reference documents and the approved answers do not answer a question,
   write exactly this sentence: "The module team will confirm this separately."
   In a German reply, write: "Das Modulteam bestätigt dies gesondert."
3. The module team does not decide on deadline extensions, illness or grades.
   Do not grant, promise or suggest such a decision. Name the examination office
   (pruefungsamt@example.edu) as the body that decides.
4. Do not give any information about other students.
5. Do not repeat matriculation numbers or other personal identifiers.
6. Reply in the language of the email.
7. Open with a salutation that uses the student's name if it is given. Close
   with "Kind regards," (German: "Mit freundlichen Grüßen") followed by
   "EDU-204 module team" on its own line.
8. Write at most 150 words. Do not write a subject line.
9. Answer the question the email asks. If the email asks several questions,
   answer each of them.
10. Copy names of courses, folders, rooms and addresses exactly as written in
    the reference documents. Do not translate them.

Reference documents:

# EDU-204 Research Methods in Education — module information, winter term 2026/27

Fictitious data, written for the llmlab exercise.

## 1 Contact and office hours

Module team: edu204@example.edu. Office hours: Tuesdays 14:00–15:30, room
G40-212, or by video call on request. Emails are answered within three working
days.

## 2 Assessment

The module is assessed by a portfolio (60 %) and a written examination (40 %).

- Portfolio submission deadline: 15 January 2027, 12:00, via the learning
  platform. Each student submits the portfolio personally from their own account.
- Written examination: 9 February 2027, 10:00–12:00, lecture hall H3.
- Resit examination: 30 March 2027, 10:00–12:00, room G40-B05.
- Registration for the written examination is required and closes on
  12 December 2026 in the campus portal.

## 3 Extensions and illness

Extensions to the portfolio deadline are granted only by the examination office
(pruefungsamt@example.edu), not by the module team. The application must be
submitted before the deadline and, in the case of illness, include a medical
certificate. Students who are ill on the day of the examination submit a medical
certificate to the examination office within three working days.

## 4 Grades and review

Results are published in the campus portal by 2 March 2027. Students can inspect
their marked examination in the review session on 5 March 2027, 13:00–15:00,
room G40-212. Requests to change a grade are submitted in writing to the
examination office within one month of publication. The module team does not
discuss grades by email.

## 5 Course materials

Readings are provided on the learning platform in the course "EDU-204 2026/27".
The reading list is in the folder "Week 0".

## 6 Data protection

The module team does not confirm or discuss the enrolment, registration, grades
or circumstances of any student with another person.

# Specification: replies to student emails, module EDU-204

You draft replies to emails that students send to the module team of EDU-204
Research Methods in Education.

Rules:

1. Use only information from the reference documents and the approved answers.
   Do not add dates, times, rooms, procedures or names that are not stated there.
2. If the reference documents and the approved answers do not answer a question,
   write exactly this sentence: "The module team will confirm this separately."

5. Do not repeat matriculation numbers or other personal identifiers.
6. Reply in the language of the email.
7. Open with a salutation that uses the student's name if it is given. Close
   with "Kind regards," (German: "Mit freundlichen Grüßen") followed by
   "EDU-204 module team" on its own line.
8. Write at most 150 words. Do not write a subject line.
9. Answer the question the email asks. If the email asks several questions,
   answer each of them.
10. Copy names of courses, folders, rooms and addresses exactly as written in
    the reference documents. Do not translate them.

certificate. Students who are ill on the day of the examination submit a medical
certificate to the examination office within three working days.

examination office within one month of publication. The module team does not
discuss grades by email.
